title: hotfix: slo-enforcer regional failover ordering edgecase
author: Ava Chen
description: Hotfix to address an ordering edgecase in the SLO enforcer that could cause regional failover to skip healthy regions during high-load failover windows. Root cause: under specific timing conditions the enforcer's backoff/quorum evaluation and the regional queue drain detection race, causing the policy executor to mark a region as 'degraded' while it was still draining requests, leading to repeated failovers and transient client errors. This change tightens the failover ordering and adds an explicit quiesce window and stronger idempotency checks for region state transitions. Changes include: 1) add quiesce_window_ms (default 300) before marking region as degraded; 2) enforce serializable region-state updates with a small compare-and-set token attached to policy events; 3) refine load_shedding threshold smoothing to avoid oscillation during bursts; 4) add unit and integration tests that simulate cross-region drain races; 5) add metrics and alerts for 'region_quiesce_misses' to detect remaining races. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce failure in perf-canary harness - [x] Tests added for race scenarios - [x] CI green on linux/amd64 and arm - [x] Metrics & dashboards updated - [x] Rollout plan: 50% canary -> 100% over 30m with rollback knobs Related: Linear ENG-7621, SRE-128, incident INC-2026-02-12. Notes: this is a hotfix; changes are backward compatible but increase the default quiesce window. Operators can tune via rollout flags. Merge plan: squash merge to main with immediate canary deploy to region us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
